Modified assessment incorporating Beige Book insights:
- Activity: Beige Book reports a modest pickup as many Districts saw rebounds in consumer spending (notably autos) and a rise in manufacturing and residential construction from very depressed levels, but overall activity remains well below pre-pandemic benchmarks.
- Sectoral mix: Strength in consumer spending and housing contrasts with ongoing weakness in commercial real estate and the energy sector; tourism/leisure and airlines remain severely constrained.
- Labor and prices: Employment increased with recalls, but total jobs remain far below earlier levels; wage pressures subdued; prices flat to modest amid supply-chain frictions.
- Credit conditions: Consistent with SLOOS, banks tightened standards broadly for C&I, CRE, and household credit even as mortgage demand is strong; this may temper the transmission of highly accommodative policy.
- Policy backdrop and risks: The FOMC maintains 0–0.25% rates and ongoing Treasury/MBS/CMBS purchases, with repo and ON RRP supporting market functioning. Outlook remains highly uncertain and dependent on the virus path.

Net tone: Cautiously negative but less so than the prior assessment given the Beige Book’s evidence of a modest rebound across several sectors, offset by tight credit supply, sectoral weakness (CRE, energy), and elevated uncertainty.
